title.en: Define scarcity and explain why it forces choice

say.en: Your family has one monthly income, but the list of things everyone wants never ends. How do you decide what to buy first? In this lesson: Explain what an economy is.
Define scarcity and explain why it forces choice.
Tell economic from non-economic activities.

body.en: An *economy* is the way a society organises the production, exchange and consumption of goods and services. People need food, clothing, shelter and services such as health and education. They use resources such as land, labour, machines and skills to produce these goods, and exchange what they produce with one another, usually through money.
body.kn: ಸಮಾಜವು ಸರಕು ಮತ್ತು ಸೇವೆಗಳ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ, ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮತ್ತು ಅನುಭೋಗವನ್ನು ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗೊಳಿಸುವ ರೀತಿಯೇ ಅರ್ಥವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆ. ಜನರು ಭೂಮಿ, ಶ್ರಮ, ಯಂತ್ರಗಳಂತಹ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲಗಳನ್ನು ಬಳಸಿ ಸರಕುಗಳನ್ನು ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸಿ ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾರೆ.

body.en: Human wants are unlimited, but the resources available to satisfy them are limited. Resources also have alternative uses: the same acre of land can grow paddy or sugarcane, and the same hour can be spent studying or working. This *scarcity* of resources relative to wants is the basic economic problem, and it forces every person and every society to choose.
body.kn: ಬಯಕೆಗಳು ಅಪರಿಮಿತ, ಆದರೆ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲಗಳು ಸೀಮಿತ ಮತ್ತು ಪರ್ಯಾಯ ಉಪಯೋಗಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿವೆ. ಈ ಅಭಾವವೇ ಎಲ್ಲ ಆರ್ಥಿಕ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗಳ ಮೂಲ; ಅದು ನಮ್ಮನ್ನು ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡುವಂತೆ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.

points.en: *Scarcity* is relative: wants exceed the resources available
Alternative uses mean every *choice* has a cost

problem.en: A farmer in Mandya has 5 acres. Paddy earns him ₹40,000 an acre and sugarcane ₹55,000 an acre, but sugarcane needs much more water. Use this to explain scarcity and choice.

steps.en: His land (5 acres) and water are limited: this is scarcity.
Each acre has alternative uses: paddy or sugarcane.
All 5 acres in sugarcane earn 5 × 55,000 = ₹2,75,000, but he gives up 5 × 40,000 = ₹2,00,000 from paddy.
Choosing one use means giving up the other: scarcity forces choice.

answer.en: Limited land with alternative uses forces a choice; the ₹2,00,000 of paddy income given up is the cost of choosing sugarcane.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A farmer in Mandya has 5 acres. Paddy earns him 40,000 rupees an acre and sugarcane 55,000 rupees an acre, but sugarcane needs much more water. Use this to explain scarcity and choice.
His land 5 acres and water are limited: this is scarcity.
Each acre has alternative uses: paddy or sugarcane.
All 5 acres in sugarcane earn 5 times 55,000 equals 2,75,000, rupees but he gives up 5 times 40,000 equals 2,00,000 rupees from paddy.
Choosing one use means giving up the other: scarcity forces choice.
So the answer is Limited land with alternative uses forces a choice; the 2,00,000 rupees of paddy income given up is the cost of choosing sugarcane.
